similar: Jonathan Richman And The Modern Lovers
info.bio: Jonathan Richman, nacido en 1951 en Boston (EE.UU.), conocido por su personalidad excéntrica, infantil y encantadora, formó en 1970 The Modern Lovers, un grupo de sonido garage. La banda se separó en 1973 para renacer después solo como grupo acústico. Tuvieron un gran éxito en Europa, "Egyptian Reggae", sacado de su segundo álbum. En 1979 Richman decidió iniciar su carrera en solitario e hizo una serie de discos que varían del country al garage pasando por ritmos latinos, siempre seguido por una audiencia fiel.

scenes.name: American Graffiti: revival, garage y power-pop
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: American Graffiti (1973) desata el revival de los cincuenta y sesenta, que suenan más auténticos que el rock corporativo de los setenta: rockabilly, surf, folk-rock, psicodelia, bandas sonoras de terror. Los punks descubren el alma malvada del rockabilly: Suicide inventa el psychobilly y los Cramps el «voodoobilly»; Fleshtones, Raybeats, Stray Cats, Von Lmo. El garage revive con Slickee Boys, Pretenders, Wipers, Real Kids; el power-pop con Cheap Trick, Shoes, Cars, Jonathan Richman y Embarrassment. En California, los Blasters y el cow-punk de Rank And File; Tom Petty como teórico del power-pop, Plimsouls, Redd Kross, Go-Go's, Bangles. El blues para la generación punk: George Thorogood, Fabulous Thunderbirds, J. Geils Band, Dixie Dregs.

podcast.title: Contrarian Persona
podcast.body: Jonathan Richman, a Boston native, presented himself as the antithesis of the prevailing big names of his era. He kept his hair short, actively opposed drug use, and was frequently heard yelling "I hate hippies" around Boston. Unlike many contemporaries who favored The Beatles, The Rolling Stones, or the growing prog rock scene, Richman preferred the raw, unconventional sound of The Velvet Underground and The Stooges, leading him to be perceived as "weird" by mainstream audiences. "Jonathan Richmond was the complete opposite of the big names of the day. He wore his hair short and he was against using drugs. He could often be heard yelling, I hate hippies around Boston."

podcast.title: Early Obscurity and Band Breakup
podcast.body: Jonathan Richman and his band, The Modern Lovers, worked in obscurity for a couple of years after recording demos like "Roadrunner" in 1971. Despite the forward-thinking nature of their music, the timing was not right for their style to gain widespread recognition. The band eventually broke up in 1974. "Jonathan and his band, the modern lovers, toiled in obscurity for a couple of years before breaking up in 1974."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Prototypical Alternative Artist (1970s)
podcast.body: Jonathan Richman is highlighted as a "prototypical alternative artist" from the 1970s, primarily because he recorded for Beserkley Records. This label was identified as an "alternative label," signifying its independence from the major record companies of the era. "His name is Jonathan Richmond and he recorded for an alternative label called Fizzerkerly."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Groundwork for Punk Rock
xref.body: The stripped-down songs of Jonathan Richman and The Modern Lovers were instrumental in laying the groundwork for punk rock, with their music frequently classified as proto-punk, meaning it predated and helped define the genre. "His stripped down songs help set the groundwork for punk rock. In fact, we classify his music as proto-punk, the stuff that had to happen first before punk rock could be born."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Peaked Too Soon - Bands That Were Ahead of Their Time

xref.title: Influence on Punk and Post-Punk
xref.body: Although Jonathan Richman and the Modern Lovers never achieved significant record sales, they were highly influential to early punk bands and many post-punk groups such as the Sex Pistols, R.E.M., Violent Femmes, Dinosaur Jr., The Cars, The Pixies, and the Ramones. This impact stemmed from Jonathan Richman being a big Velvet Underground fan. "Jonathan Richmond and the Modern Lovers never sold a lot of records, but they were very important to the early punks and many of the post-punk bands like the Sex Pistols and REM and the Violent Femmes and Dinosaur Jr. and the Cars and the Pixies and the Ramones."

xref.title: Movie Appearance - There's Something About Mary
xref.body: Jonathan Richman made notable appearances in the movie "There's Something About Mary," where he was featured as the guitarist who pops up in various strange places throughout the film. "And if you remember the movie, there's something about Mary. Jonathan is the guy with a guitar who shows up in strain places during the film."

xref.title: Obscurity and Breakup
xref.body: The Modern Lovers, fronted by Jonathan Richman, toiled in obscurity for several years. Despite their distinctive sound, which was ahead of its time, they did not achieve widespread recognition. The band ultimately broke up in 1974. "Jonathan and his band, the modern lovers, toiled in obscurity for a couple of years before breaking up in 1974."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Velvet Underground Fanatic
xref.body: Jonathan Richman was a "hardcore velvet underground fan," directly inspired by their music to pursue a career in music himself. "Jonathan Richmond was inspired to get into music because, like I said, of the Velvet Underground."
